newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee retraces after setting contract highs.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee retraces after setting contract highs.

text.p: CSCE coffee prices drew back from fresh contract highs set this morning, as commodity funds swept in to take profits on the rally, trading sources said.

Fueled by renewed supply worries following the start of a long-planned truckers' strike in Colombia over the weekend, benchmark July futures shot up by nearly five cents at the opening, to 199 cents a lb. But overall volume was fairly thin, traders said, and speculative selling quickly braked the run-up.
"The strike in Colombia scared a lot of people," said one broker. "But we got a lot of profit-taking."
By mid-morning, July retreated to 195.75 cents, up 1.60 from Friday's close. Spot May, which goes into notice period tomorrow, was 0.95 cent higher as of 1056 EDT, at 217.50, off a peak of 224.

While news of the truckers' strike in Colombia suggested supply woes would continue for some time, traders said the end of a two-day work stoppage by port workers in Brazil late last week appeared to have calmed traders' nerves.

Some coffee was reported to be backed up at Brazilian ports awaiting shipment, but the overall impact on on supply was muted, traders said. Brazil and Colombia are the world's number one and two coffee producers.

On the charts, May futures would need to hold the 217 level to remain bullish in the near-term. A shift into negative territory could provoke a test of the 213 mark, traders said. Resistance was noted at this morning's highs, with 220.00 cents in July seen as a crucial chart barrier.
((-- W Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
